subject.title: ACP parent session stuck until refresh when yielded waiting for child completion

question: Should yielded-parent resumption be one core runtime contract across ACP and native subagents, or should maintainers land only the current narrow recovery slices?
rationale: Current main has partial repairs and open candidate PRs, but the complete behavior spans runtime ownership across ACP, native subagents, task registry delivery, and heartbeat wake behavior.

options.title: Define one core wake contract
options.body: Treat this issue as the canonical contract and require candidate PRs to compose into heartbeat-independent yielded-parent resumption across ACP and native subagents.

options.title: Land narrow slices only
options.body: Accept the open PRs as incremental mitigations and leave broader native/ACP edge cases to separate issue-specific follow-ups.

options.title: Reject Phase B for now
options.body: Do not add dedicated yield-wait semantics yet, and document heartbeat/polling limitations as current behavior.

recommendation.title: Define one core wake contract
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the canonical contract and require candidate PRs to compose into heartbeat-independent yielded-parent resumption across ACP and native subagents.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the best available routing owner from current blame across the central source files, with other likely owners contributing to ACP and native subagent slices.
